title: The Untranslatable Remainder
text:
Every literary translator confronts a stubborn residue that resists transfer from one language to another. Idioms, rhythm, and the connotations of a single adjective often refuse to survive the journey intact. Consequently, the translator must decide whether to prioritize fidelity to the original's letter or to its effect on the reader. Many critics argue that this tension is not a failure but the very condition that makes translation a creative act.

Consider a poem whose meter depends on the stresses of its source tongue; a faithful rendering may sound clumsy, while a fluent one may quietly discard the original's music. Some translators compensate by inventing new images that were never present in the source. Such liberties are controversial, yet they reveal how deeply meaning is bound to form. Ultimately, the translated text becomes a second original, shaped by the sensibility of the person who wrote it.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what often fails to survive translation?
options: The length of the original text

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say the meter of a poem depends on?
options: The stresses of its source tongue
The length of its final stanza

questions.text: What does the author imply about a translation that is only fluent?
options: It may lose the original's musical qualities
It is always more accurate than a literal version
It is usually preferred by the original author
It cannot be published in another language

questions.text: What is the author's overall view of translation?
options: It is a creative act that produces a second original
It is a purely mechanical task with fixed rules
It should always be avoided in favor of the original
It mainly serves to correct errors in the source text

vocabulary.definition: a small amount left over after the main part has gone
the additional meanings a word carries beyond its literal sense
to make up for a shortcoming

paragraph_translations: Her edebi çevirmen, bir dilden diğerine aktarılmaya direnen inatçı bir kalıntıyla karşılaşır. Deyimler, ritim ve tek bir sıfatın taşıdığı çağrışımlar çoğu zaman yolculuğu bozulmadan atlatamaz. Bu nedenle çevirmen, orijinalin harfine mi yoksa okur üzerindeki etkisine mi öncelik vereceğine karar vermek zorundadır. Pek çok eleştirmen, bu gerilimin bir başarısızlık değil, çeviriyi yaratıcı bir eylem kılan temel koşul olduğunu savunur.

Ölçüsü kaynak dilin vurgularına dayanan bir şiiri düşünün; sadık bir çeviri kulağa sert gelebilirken, akıcı bir çeviri orijinalin müziğini sessizce yitirebilir. Bazı çevirmenler, kaynak metinde hiç bulunmayan yeni imgeler icat ederek bunu telafi eder. Bu tür özgürlükler tartışmalıdır, yine de anlamın biçime ne kadar sıkı bağlı olduğunu ortaya koyar. Sonuçta çeviri metin, onu yazan kişinin duyarlılığıyla şekillenen ikinci bir orijinal haline gelir.
